column1: # What each display-generator request does, one line each (older rows are five words or fewer), written by hand from the handler readings
# in software/ucode/arm1_functions.md (arm1.u, IRIX 6.5.30m). scripts/dg_requests.py joins it with DGDispatchTable.

column2: effect
reads payload word 0, adds one and sends the sum back as a one-word reply, a loop-back check of the command path that touches no hardware
writes payload word 1 to the display-bus word indexed by payload word 0, ARM address 0x600000 plus four times the index, between short delay loops and with no range check
reads any display-bus word

packs a colour from payload words 0-9 into two 32-bit words, in a layout chosen by word 7 (or word 8 when it is 1), and writes them to every XMAP chip selected by the mask in word 9: it writes 1 to display-bus word 0x105 to turn the substitute colour on, then for each selected chip the chip number to 0x108 and the packed words to 0x106 and 0x107, and forces an XMAP copy-buffer update
writes 0 to XMAP register 0x105, which turns the diagnostic substitute colour off, between delay loops and then forces an XMAP copy-buffer update; reads no payload
prints a message that bus tracing was not compiled in and returns; it ignores its four payload words and touches no hardware

writes payload word 0 to bus word 0x118, sends the 64 by 64 two-bit image (one pixel per payload word, last row first) to port 0x119 as two bit planes, four words per row, then three colour words packed from ten-bit fields at the payload end (two words read past it) and one unwritten stack word, and ends with a short count sequence to ports 0x11f and 0x11e
stores payload word 0 as the firmware debug-print mask in the first word of the display state and prints the new value; no hardware access and no reply

converts payload word 0 (width) to a tile count of 160 pixels, rounding up, stores it at state offset 0x36b4 and multiplies by the height in word 1 to size the frame; reads the raster-board count from display-bus register 0x10b, compares a capacity derived from that count with the frame size and, when the board option word is not 6, warns and sets bit 28 of the status word at 0x0406cd1c if the count is too small; stores a pixel-size code at state offset 0x36b8 chosen from payload word 2 and the board count (a word 2 outside the table's range prints an illegal-pixel-depth warning); writes width, height and code as byte pairs at state offsets 0x40-0x45
read-modify-writes bits 21-20 of display-bus register 0x8b with the low two bits of payload word 0, which pick the input sync source
reads register 0x8b bits 21-20

converts the phase in payload word 1 (hundredths of a pixel) into a coarse count of clock groups, a wrapped second count and a fine 8-bit value from the record's line length and pixels per group, saves the phase at record +0x16c, writes the counts to VOC registers 0x0c and 0x0d with bits 8-4 of register 0x06 set to 9, and the fine value to gain-DAC slot 1 for channels 0-7; the three encoder channels take fixed counts and, when not the master, a delay word at ARM address 0x633000; channel 0x5e with record +0x180 equal to 1 is sent a VBOB packet in place of the VOC writes
replies with the horizontal phase last stored for the channel named by payload word 0, the word at channel record offset 0x16c, as a four-byte reply of type 3

decodes payload word 0 as a signed vertical phase with the channel number plus one in its top ten bits; it stores the value in the shared slot for all channels or channel 1, or in the channel record at offset 0x168, and applies it through the vertical-phase adjuster
replies with the vertical phase last stored, the shared slot at display-state offset 0x36cc for channel 1 and otherwise the channel record word at offset 0x168, as a four-byte reply of type 4

sets bit 25 of the channel control word when payload word 1 is -2, meaning no gamma map; any other value clears the bit and stores the map index at record offset 0x170, then XMAP channel-format register 0x11d is updated
replies with the gamma-map index at record offset 0x170 of the channel named by payload word 0, as a four-byte reply of type 5, without a range check on the channel

ignores its payload and rebuilds the default state: clears counters, fills bus words 0-0x3f with 0x20, then 0x40-0x5f with zero, clears three 4096-word XMAP banks, builds a channel record and the block defaults for each present VOC and option channel with a warning for each mismatch against the expected configuration, runs the option-board builder for the board type, puts a board code in bus word 0x90, and ends by writing all ones then zero to bus word 0
builds the five-word board-configuration record on the stack through the configuration reader and sends it as a 20-byte reply of type 6; reads no hardware itself
returns 0x4c-byte channel description
calls the channel resize routine with the eight payload words; when other channels copy this one (record offset 0xbc above zero) it applies the same resize to every dependent channel
replies with 18 words of the channel resize state, the record words 0x50-0x6f and the placement words and bits 23 and 22 of the control word at offset 0x184, as a 72-byte reply of type 8

loads one video format: disables the channel, copies the format's summary words into the channel record, loads both clock parameter sets and starts the VOC clock, streams the sequencer words, 32 register pairs and the 50 edge words of the edge-group table into the VOC, loads partner channels by recursion, sets the blanking, FIFO and pixel-multiplex fields, runs the field-sequential, stereo and XMAP format routines and writes the vertical registers; it does not enable the channel

turns a channel on from payload word 0 (channel), word 1 (turn-on flag) and word 2 (set-up flag): a set-up flag, when bit 0 of VOC register 0x06 is set, writes 0 to register 0x02 first and 1 last, and in between writes a FIFO threshold from the record width (0x370 for widths up to 1024) to register 0x8a of the channel and its partner ids and starts the requester; a turn-on flag copies register 0x01 with its low two bits cleared and register 0x06 with bit 0 set to the write VOC after syncing to the master VOC, and sets bit 28 of the record flag word for the channel and its partners

turns a channel off: clears bits 1-0 of VOC register 0x01 and bit 0 of register 0x06 on the channel's write VOC, with short delay loops between the writes, clears the enabled bit 28 in the channel record flag word and in the partner option-board record where one exists, then tail-calls the requester routine with its on flag zero
hands the 16-word payload to the per-channel genlock-parameter writer for every present video-output chip; it is a tail call with no hardware access of its own

blanks all channels, shuts down the requesters on every present VOC and waits; when payload word 0 is zero it reprograms each channel's genlock clocks and waits again; it then sets every channel's genlock to the payload value, copies its low bit into bit 31 of the display-state flag word at 0x0406cd1c, waits, restarts the requesters and unblanks
combines the 13-bit horizontal position in payload word 0 with the vertical position in word 1 shifted into bits 25-13 and writes the result to XMAP cursor register 0x102
looks up the channel record named by payload word 0 and writes its first word, the channel index, to XMAP register 0x100, choosing which channel owns the hardware cursor
writes XMAP register 0x103 with 2 for payload value zero and 1 for payload value one; any other value writes zero, cursor off, and no state is kept

stores payload word 1, the cursor priority, at offset 4 of the channel record named by payload word 0, with no range check and no display register write, so only the firmware's own record changes; sends no reply

masks payload word 1 to one bit and merges it into bit 31 of the channel record's flag word at offset 0x184 for the channel in payload word 0; then calls the blanking routine for that channel only when the shared all-channel blank counter at display-state offset 0x36d0 is zero; nothing is sent back to the host
replies with the channel blank bit, bit 31 of the record control word at offset 0x184, or with 1 when the shared blanking-depth word at display-state offset 0x36d0 is above zero

sets the output gain of a video DAC channel (ids 0-7 or 0xde, anything else returns) from the low byte of payload word 1: stores the gain in the channel record at +0x15c and writes 255 minus the gain to the gain DAC through the channel writer; channel 1 with the encoder-drive bit 26 set in its flag word instead stores the gain at state offset 0x36bc and writes 255 minus the gain to display-bus register 0x1708
replies with the output gain: for channel 1 with bit 26 of its control word set the shared word at display-state offset 0x36bc, otherwise the record word at offset 0x15c

sets one sync-output option picked by payload word 1: on video DAC channels a bit of control register 6 or of register 8, record flag bit 29 with the inverse in gain-DAC slot 2, or (channel 1 only) bits 14-13 of the mode word at bus word 0x8400, then bit 0 of register 8 from word 3 and a recomputed gain select; option-board channels take only the record bit with bit 6 of the option word, or bits 5-3 of that word from word 2
returns six sync options

for channel 1 first passes payload word 1 to the encoder pedestal routine; for channels 0 to 7 it then reads video-DAC control register 6, replaces bit 3 with bit 0 of payload word 1, writes it back and recomputes the DAC gain select; other channel numbers do nothing further; no reply
reads video-DAC control register 6 for a channel numbered 0-7 and replies with its bit 3, the pedestal enable, or with -1 for any other channel number

writes 0 to display-bus word 0x118 (ARM address 0x00600460) and then 0x80050 to word 0x11c (0x00600470), each write preceded and followed by a three-pass delay loop; reads no payload and sends no reply

clears display-bus words 0x101 and 0x100, sets word 0x103 to 2 and clears word 0x118, then copies the 260 words of the firmware's textport glyph buffer one by one to word 0x119 (ARM address 0x00600464), a delay loop after each; reads no payload and sends no reply

takes the low ten bits of payload word 3 as bits 9-0 of one word, of word 2 as bits 19-10 and of word 1 as bits 29-20; writes payload word 0 plus 0x1000 to display-bus word 0x118, then the packed word to word 0x119, with delay loops around each write; no reply

loads a fixed clock-parameter set built on the stack into the chip named by payload word 0 with the clock-parameter loader, restarts that chip's clock with mode 0, then sets bit 1 of the chip's word at ARM address 0x00600910 plus 0x400 times the chip number, after a three-pass delay loop and followed by a second; no reply

replaces bit 23 of display-bus word 0x8e (ARM address 0x00600238) with 1 when payload word 0 equals 1 and 0 otherwise, after a three-pass delay loop, then stores payload word 0 at display-state offset 0x36c4 for the matching query; no reply
replies with a four-byte word, reply type 0xd, loaded from display-state offset 0x36c4 (0x0406cd18); the word is the master-clock select the set request stored, and no display register is read

clears the first word of the display state, reads an eight-byte header from the EEPROM at 0x20000 and accepts it when word 0 is 0xfacefeed and word 1, the length, is non-negative and below 0x8000; accepted: reads length plus 2 words, clears bit 28 of the display-state word at offset 0x36c8 and runs the stored combination through the combination loader; if that sets bit 28 or returns zero it prints a message and rebuilds the default state, then falls to the built-in emergency format of 0x3fe words; a rejected header goes straight to the emergency format; a failed emergency load prints "combination load failed"; no reply

programs the video encoder through the encoder control writer: clears register 0 twice and rewrites it from the master-clock-select word, puts fixed values in the mode, clock and sync registers with bit 2 of register 2 from payload word 0, loads one of two fixed 19-value tables into registers 0x10-0x23 (0x1f skipped) chosen by the master-clock-select word, and ends with registers 0x26 and 0x27. The first table goes out when that word is zero and the second when it is not, and only the second leaves 0x20 in register 0x27.
keeps the low byte of payload word 0 in display-state offset 0x36bc and writes 255 minus that byte to display-bus word 0x1708 (ARM address 0x00605c20), between delay loops; no reply

replies with a four-byte word, reply type 0xe, loaded from display-state offset 0x36bc (0x0406cd10); the word is the encoder output gain the encoder-gain request stored, and no display register is read

writes the low byte of payload word 0 to encoder register 0x24 and its next byte to 0x25; then adds 0x2000 to the word and writes the low byte of the sum to register 0x26 and the next byte to 0x27; nothing is sent back to the host
reads encoder register 0x24 as the low byte and register 0x25 as the high byte, combines them into one 16-bit value and replies with it as a four-byte reply of type 0xf

reads encoder register 1, clears bit 5 and sets bit 4, then clears bit 4 when payload word 0 is 1 or sets bit 5 when it is 2, and writes the result back to register 1; any other payload leaves bit 4 set and bit 5 clear

stores payload word 1, the window id, in the per-channel table at display-state offset 0x368c; when the id is zero it also calls the resize handler (request 20) with eight words built from the record's four rectangle words at offsets 0x60 to 0x6c, bits 23 and 22 of the control word at 0x184 and a final zero; a non-zero id returns after the store

loads the display board's programmable logic serially from 1328 payload words: runs the clear and wait-clear routines, shifts out six header bytes least-significant bit first through the bit writer, then word 1 frames of word 2 bits each with a frame check after every frame, shifts the remaining bytes, runs the done check and on success reads the word at ARM address 0x609400; prints a failure message when a check fails; word 0 is the byte count and the data starts at word 3
writes payload words 0 to 3 in order, unmodified, to display-bus words 0x2300 to 0x2303 (ARM addresses 0x00608c00 to 0x00608c0c), each write followed by a three-pass delay loop; no reply
writes payload word 0 unmodified to display-bus word 0x2304 (ARM address 0x00608c10) between two three-pass delay loops; payload word 1 is never read, no reply

loads a video DAC's hardware cursor from 263 payload words, accepted for channels 0-7 and 0xde only: writes select index 0x0303 to the DAC's select port as two bytes, the six colour words to its data port, then select index 0x0400, and streams 1024 image bytes, four from each of the 256 image words low byte first

for channel 0x1e copies bit 31 of payload word 4 into bit 9 of the record's flag word at offset 0x88; for every channel it then clears bit 31 of payload word 4 in place and jumps to the vampire handler (request 79) to process the payload; no hardware write of its own

for the channel in payload word 0 copies six words from its record into a reply buffer, the word at offset 0x4c, the pair at 0x80, then the three words from 0xd0, and sends them unchanged as a 24-byte reply of type 0x10; the read-back of request 79, no hardware access
ORs the low five bits of payload word 0 with 0x320 and writes the result to display-bus word 0x10f (ARM address 0x0060043c) between two three-pass delay loops; no reply

nests an all-channel blank: a nonzero payload adds one to the counter at display-state offset 0x36d0 and, if the old value was zero or negative, blanks every present video-output chip; a zero payload subtracts one, floors a negative result at zero and, if the result is not above zero, unblanks every present chip through the blanking routine; no reply
returns 12-byte interrupt state

returns at once when payload word 0 equals the word stored at display-state offset 0x36c0; for any value other than zero or one it tail-calls the printf routine with a message naming the unknown XMapClockSelect value and stores nothing; otherwise it writes the value to ARM address 0x00606400 when the board-type word at 0x04067edc is zero, or to 0x00620000 when it is not, with delay loops, and stores it at 0x36c0; no reply
replies with a four-byte word, reply type 0x12, loaded from display-state offset 0x36c0 (0x0406cd14); the word is the colour-map clock select the set request stored, and no display register is read
stores payload word 1 at offset 0x9c of the channel record named by payload word 0, then payload word 2 at offset 0xa0; firmware state only, no hardware access and no reply

prints a start message, nests an all-channel blank, stops the requesters on every present chip, clears bits 1-0 of display-bus word 0x301 and bit 0 of word 0x306, sleeps, prints a message, resets the image-processor chips, prints a second message, sets bit 0 of word 0x306 again, sleeps, restarts the requesters on every present chip, sleeps, ends the blank and prints a completion message; bits 1-0 of word 0x301 stay clear; no reply
replies with two words from the record control word at offset 0x184: first bit 28, the enabled flag, then bit 27, as an eight-byte reply of type 0x13

stores payload words 1 to 4 at offsets 0xc0 up to 0xcc and payload words 5 to 8 at offsets 0x70 up to 0x7c, each at 4-byte steps, of the channel record named by payload word 0, unmodified; touches no hardware and sends no reply
copies bit 0 of payload word 0 into bit 30 of the display-state flag word at 0x0406cd1c, the genlock-switching flag, leaving the other bits alone; no hardware write and no reply
pulses 0x343 bit 0, replies

reads the channel's field-select word at ARM address 0x00600a3c plus 0x400 times the channel, replaces bit 9 with bit 0 of payload word 1 (cleared instead for channels 0x1e and 0x1f when the board-revision test on 0x04068608 passes) and writes it back after a three-pass delay loop, keeping the same value in record offset 0x88; no reply
replies with bit 9 of the channel record word at offset 0x88, the field-dominance flag, as a four-byte reply of type 0x15
reads display-bus word 0x8b (ARM address 0x0060022c), replaces bit 22 with bit 0 of payload word 0 and writes it back after a three-pass delay loop, followed by a second delay; no reply
reads register 0x8b bit 22

replies with five words, type 0x17, for the channel in payload word 0: the pixel-format word at record offset 0xac, bit 30 of the control word at offset 0x184, bit 26 of that word, the constant -1, then the word at record offset 0x164; every value comes from the firmware's channel record, none from the display hardware

for payload word 0 equal to -1 copies bit 0 of payload word 1 into bit 29 of the shared state word at display-state offset 0x36c8 and payload words 2 to 4 into the three words at 0x36d4; for ids 0 to 7 and 0x1e to 0xfd it copies that bit into bit 25 of the channel record's control word at offset 0x184 and the three words into record offset 0x174; any other id returns with nothing stored; firmware state only, no reply

replies with four words, type 0x18: a flag followed by the three words request 75 stored; for channel -1 the flag is bit 29 of the word at display-state offset 0x36c8 and the words come from 0x36d4; for ids from 0 up to 7, and from 0x1e up to 0xfd, the flag is bit 25 of the record's control word at offset 0x184 and the words come from record offset 0x174; any other id sends a zero flag; no hardware access

builds encoder control register 0 as bit 0 and bit 4 both equal to bit 0 of payload word 0, bit 3 set when the master-clock-select word at display-state offset 0x36c4 is zero, all other bits zero; writes that value to the register twice; nothing is sent back to the host

sets bit 24 of the channel record's control word at offset 0x184 to 1 when payload word 1 equals 1 and to 0 for any other value, for the channel in payload word 0; firmware state only, no hardware write and no reply

makes one channel copy another's output: decrements the old source's dependent count at record offset 0xbc and increments the new source's, stores the source channel at +0x4c, copies the output width and height from payload words 2-3 to +0x80-0x84 and the field layout from word 4 to +0xd0; a nonzero filter size in word 5 or 6 is stored with bit 0 set at +0xd4 or +0xd8, and a zero in either word stores 0; channel 1 then runs the encoder letterbox when bit 26 of its flag word is set, and the digital output channels run the output letterbox
returns 0x44-byte monitor identity
a single return instruction; the dispatch table passes it 34 payload words but it reads none of them; it changes no hardware or firmware state and sends nothing back
loads option-board logic image

when a first board word is nonzero and the board option word is 6, writes 1 then 0 to display-bus register 0xc000 with delay loops and sleeps between; then walks the 17 option VOC entries and rebuilds the default state of each one marked for rebuild and present (a present one that does not match the board option prints a warning, as does one that should be present and is missing); finishes by tail-calling the late-channel auto-initialisation
copies bit 0 of payload word 0 into bit 27 of the display-state flag word at 0x0406cd1c, the internal-genlock flag, leaving the other bits alone; no hardware write and no reply
replies with bit 27 of the display status word at 0x0406cd1c, the internal genlock flag, as a four-byte reply of type 0x1c

merges bit 0 of payload word 1 into bit 21 of the channel record's control word at offset 0x184 and, for every channel except 0x5e, stores payload word 2 unchanged at record offset 0x180; firmware records only, no hardware write and no reply
replies with two words, bit 21 of the record control word at offset 0x184 and then the record word at offset 0x180, as an eight-byte reply of type 0x1d

stores the format code at record +0xb0 and record flag bit 20 from a zero flag word, then by channel id programs the option board: ids 0x5e-0x60 set bits 12-11 of the mode word at bus word 0x8400 to 1 and send serial-bus device 0xee a byte mapped from the format; ids 0xc9-0xca and 0xd9 set those bits to 2, as does id 0xde, which also writes three more registers; the digital video output ids write their control registers, a two-word encoder image and 13-bit coefficients from one of two ten-entry tables chosen by the format

replies with two words, type 0x1e: the data-format code at offset 0xb0 of the channel record named by payload word 0, then 1 when bit 20 of the record's control word at offset 0x184 is clear and 0 when it is set; every value comes from the firmware's channel record, none from the display hardware

replaces bit 7 of the option board's register with bit 0 of payload word 0, read-modify-write after a three-pass delay loop and followed by a second delay; the register is the word at ARM address 0x0060d000 (display-bus word 0x3400) when the board-type word at 0x04067edc is zero and 0x00633400 (word 0xcd00) otherwise; no reply

sends a packet to the option board over the two-wire bus at port 0xa000: a start to address 0xee, then payload word 0 plus 2 as the length byte, a zero byte, payload word 1, and payload words 2 onward for as many words as word 0 gives, one byte each, then a stop; no reply; also the routine the channel-0x5e phase handlers call

reads a reply from the VBOB option board over the serial bus at 0xa000: two one-byte reads into the same byte, so the second is the status, where zero or 0xef gives length 0; otherwise a second transfer with one discarded read, then the status byte as the length clamped to 0x28 and that many bytes, one per word, with the last-byte flag raised on the read at index length minus 2; the reply is a record of 0xa4 bytes holding the length word and bytes, with length 0 after a read error
